claims.text: The target material class is multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states at or near their high melting temperatures.
A machine-learning-based approach can improve representation of atomic configurations in ab initio liquids of multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Improved representation of liquid atomic configurations will improve overlap between the reference and target phase spaces.
A machine-learning-based approach can predict phase stability in high-entropy alloys.
A machine-learning-based approach can predict structural evolution in high-entropy alloys.
High-entropy-alloy phase stability and structural evolution depend on composition and temperature.
The proposed approach is applicable across multicomponent high-entropy-alloy compositions at and near their high melting temperatures.
TOR-TILD uses EAM references as the relevant baseline.
The machine-learning approach will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The magnitude of the reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch is unknown and requires further research.
Free energy can be used to benchmark the predictive power of the machine-learning approach.
Failure to accurately predict free energy would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to accurately predict phase stability would falsify the hypothesis.
